note: Text for the Briefing page. Wrap a key term in {{double braces}} to color-code it. Use sparingly.
headline: Bring your squad into {{The Phantom Pain}}. Up to {{16 players}}.
summary: Joint Operations adds online multiplayer to the single-player game. The host runs the missions. Up to 15 clients share the session: the same open world, the same missions and the same Mother Base.
It's free, it's open source, and it never touches Konami's servers.
how: The host's game runs the missions, the enemies and the world. There is one version of events, so every client sees the same thing.
Every client controls their own character and camera. Their moves go to the host, and the world comes back to them.
No ports to open, no extra accounts and no Konami servers. A direct connection is there as a backup.

host.text: The {{host}} runs the session and holds every command position:

alert.title: One shared alert
alert.text: Enemies react to each player on their own, by distance and by who they actually see. The alert is shared: there is one status for the whole session, and players join it.
states: Not noticed. Most players stay here while someone else is in trouble.
Enemies are looking. A player who draws suspicion joins the search.
Spotted. A detected player joins the one detection pipeline, and every player spotted after them joins the same one.
alert.foot: So if one player is detected, only that player is hunted. If a second player is spotted, they join the same alert, not a new one.
